name: write_module_source
description: Writes BSL source into a 1C metadata object module. Eight modes: searchReplace (locate oldSource in the file and swap in source; the default), replace (overwrite the whole module), append (add text at the end), replaceLines (overwrite a range of lines), replaceMethod (swap out one method found by name), replaceMethods (atomic multi-method swap via methods[]; every target must be found or nothing is written), insertBefore (place source ahead of line N), insertAfter (place source right after line N). Identify the target via modulePath, or via objectName plus moduleType. Before the write, a BSL syntax pass verifies that Procedure/EndProcedure, Function/EndFunction, If/EndIf and similar pairs stay balanced - any mismatch blocks the write. Pass skipSyntaxCheck=true to override it. Set dryRun=true to preview the outcome without writing anything.

projectName.description: Name of the EDT project to work in

modulePath.description: Path to the module from the src/ folder, e.g. 'CommonModules/MyModule/Module.bsl' or 'Documents/MyDoc/ObjectModule.bsl'; a leading 'src/' is stripped. A write refuses a misspelled kind folder or an object the configuration does not hold, naming the canonical path. Or supply objectName + moduleType instead.

objectName.description: The object's fully-qualified name, e.g. 'Document.MyDoc' or 'DataProcessor.MyProcessor'. Metadata names in Russian work too (e.g. 'Документ.МойДок'). An alternative to modulePath.

moduleType.description: Which kind of module (paired with objectName): ObjectModule (default), ManagerModule, FormModule, CommandModule, RecordSetModule.

source.description: The BSL text to write (aliases accepted: content, sourceCode, code, text). Needed for every mode EXCEPT replaceMethods (there, each method brings its own source inside the methods[] array). For replace: the module's entire new content. For searchReplace: what to put in place of oldSource. For append: the text being added. For replaceMethod/replaceMethods: the full method, start to finish (Procedure/Function ... EndProcedure/EndFunction). If source opens with a // header comment, it takes the place of the method's existing header comment (never leaving a duplicate); when there is no leading comment, whatever header was already there is left alone. To drop an existing header comment without putting in a new one, use searchReplace instead.

oldSource.description: The fragment to find and swap out (required for searchReplace mode). It has to match exactly one spot in the file - which is also proof you actually read the current file contents.

mode.description: Picks the write mode: 'searchReplace' (find oldSource and swap in source; the default), 'replace' (overwrite the entire file), 'append' (add text at the end), 'replaceLines' (overwrite a range of lines), 'replaceMethod' (swap out one named method end-to-end), 'replaceMethods' (atomic multi-method swap - see methods[]; every target must be found, or nothing gets written), 'insertBefore' (drop source ahead of line N), 'insertAfter' (drop source right after line N).

formName.description: The form's name; required when moduleType=FormModule (e.g. 'ItemForm').

commandName.description: The command's name; required when moduleType=CommandModule (e.g. 'FillByTemplate').

lineFrom.description: Starting line number for replaceLines mode (1-based, inclusive)

lineTo.description: Ending line number for replaceLines mode (1-based, inclusive)

expectedText.description: An optional safety net for replaceLines: paste in what you believe currently sits on lines lineFrom..lineTo. If it does not match (the module changed since you last read it, so the line numbers are stale), the edit gets REJECTED and you get an expected-vs-actual diff back instead of a silent overwrite of the wrong lines. Strongly recommended - echo back the lines you plan to replace.

methodName.description: The method's name for replaceMethod mode (looked up as a Procedure/Function by that name). The span being replaced also picks up any preceding &-directives, plus the old // header comment when the new source itself opens with one.

methods.description: In replaceMethods mode, supply a JSON array of {methodName, source} objects, for instance [{"methodName":"ПриСоздании","source":"Процедура ПриСоздании()\n...\nКонецПроцедуры"}, {"methodName":"ПриЗаписи","source":"..."}]. Every referenced method has to already exist, or the call writes nothing (all-or-nothing). Per entry, 'name' works as an alias for methodName, and content/sourceCode/code/text are all accepted as aliases for source.

line.description: 1-based line number for insertBefore/insertAfter. insertBefore: source is placed right before line N (the old line N moves down to N+sourceLines). insertAfter: source is placed right after line N (the old line N+1 moves further down).

dryRun.description: Shows what the write would produce without touching the file. Reports diff stats (linesBefore, linesAfter, removedLines, addedLines)

normalizeInvalidCharacters.description: Replaces dashes, no-break spaces and soft hyphens outside string literals with plain characters and reports where. Default: true.

skipSyntaxCheck.description: Bypasses the BSL syntax check (default: false). At the default, it confirms balanced Procedure/EndProcedure, Function/EndFunction, If/EndIf, While/EndDo, For/EndDo, Try/EndTry pairs. Set true to push the write through regardless.

validateAfterWrite.description: Runs EDT validation right after a successful write and folds the outcome into the response (default: true). Adds a 'validation' section with errors / warnings / codeStyle counts, plus a short hint. Pass false while writing in a batch and call get_project_errors once at the very end instead.

confirmFullReplace.description: Has to be true when a write would strip away more than 50% of an existing module's lines. Prevents accidentally wiping out hundreds of lines when the goal was only to touch one method or fragment. Removals above 30% still proceed but come back with a non-blocking 'protection' warning. Applies to every mode that can remove lines - searchReplace, replaceLines, replaceMethod, replaceMethods and replace (a replace that strips more than half of the existing module still has to be confirmed, so an accidental stub replacement cannot silently wipe a large module); the additive modes (append, insertBefore, insertAfter) only add lines and are never gated.
